prompt: A tennis ball is hit and follows a curved projectile path through the air. Air resistance is negligible. Which statement correctly describes the directions of the velocity vector v and the acceleration vector a at an arbitrary point while the ball is descending?
options: v is directed along the tangent to the curve downwards and forwards; a is directed vertically downwards.
v is directed along the tangent to the curve downwards and forwards; a is directed along the tangent to the curve downwards.
v is directed horizontally forwards; a is directed vertically downwards.
v is directed along the tangent to the curve downwards and forwards; a is directed perpendicularly to the curve.

answer.explanation: The instantaneous velocity vector is always directed along the tangent to the trajectory in the direction of motion. In the absence of air resistance, the acceleration is solely due to gravity, which is directed vertically downwards at every point along the trajectory.

distractor_explanations: Correct. Velocity is tangential to the path, while acceleration is solely due to gravity and points vertically downwards.
Incorrect. Mistakenly assumes acceleration points in the same direction as velocity along the path.
Incorrect. Mistakenly assumes velocity is purely horizontal when descending.
Incorrect. Confuses projectile motion with circular motion where centripetal acceleration is normal to the path.
hints: What is the direction of the velocity vector for any object moving along a curved path?
What force acts on a projectile when air resistance is negligible, and in which direction does it act?
solution: A. v is directed along the tangent to the curve downwards and forwards; a is directed vertically downwards.
teacher_walkthrough: Step 1: The velocity vector is always tangent to the trajectory in the direction of motion.
Step 2: Identify the forces acting on the ball: only weight acting downwards.
Step 3: From Newton's second law, acceleration is in the direction of the resultant force, so acceleration is directed vertically downwards at all points.
